newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Breakaway Khmer Rouge seen joining army this year.
newsitem.headline: Breakaway Khmer Rouge seen joining army this year.

text.p: Khmer Rouge fighters loyal to dissident leader Ieng Sary will integrate with Cambodian government forces by the end of the year, a guerrilla commander said on Monday.

Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen is scheduled to meet Ieng Sary, foreign minister during Pol Pot's brutal 1975-79 Khmer Rouge regime, during a landmark visit on Tuesday to this gem-mining and logging centre near the border with Thailand.
Sok Peap, commander of the breakaway Division 450, told Reuters Hun Sen's visit would not include negotiations, but he expected the guerrillas to merge with the royal armed forces by late December.
"It will happen by the end of this year," he said.

The commander arrived in Pailin early Monday from his base at Phnom Malai further north to wrap up preparations for the arrival of Hun Sen, who is scheduled to spend part of Tuesday meeting villagers and soldiers.
Three government generals confirmed that Tuesday's visit was not an induction ceremony or negotiation but rather an opportunity for the two sides to welcome each other.
Hok Lundi, national police chief, said 150 police officers and 300 soldiers had been brought into Pailin to provide security for the second prime minister's visit.

First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh has already been to Pailin, flying in on October 11 for a three-hour visit and informal meeting with Ieng Sary, who broke with hardliners loyal to Pol Pot in August and forged a ceasefire with the government.
King Norodom Sihanouk last month granted an amnesty to Ieng Sary who had been sentenced to death in 1979 for his role in the genocide of more than one million people under Maoist Khmer Rouge rule.

The amnesty paved the way for the launch of talks on a military merger, government sovereignty over dissident areas and access to such places as Pailin, whose natural resources long bankrolled the Khmer Rouge war machine.
The talks are proceeding slowly, however. Impatience with the breakaway guerrillas has been offset to some extent by the defections of hundreds of guerrillas direct to the government since October 1.

In a sign of increasing cooperation between the breakaway faction and the royal coalition administration, 30 villagers were allowed to leave Pailin on Sunday to lead new lives in government-controlled zones of Battambang province.
Mok Dara, deputy police chief in Battambang, said it was the first time people from Pailin had been allowed to settle elsewhere.

The picturesque but war-battered town was a hive of industry late on Sunday as construction workers toiled through the night to renovate an old hotel where Hun Sen will meet Ieng Sary and his commanders, Khmer Rouge soldiers said.
Khmer Rouge soldiers wielding portable electric pruning machines were seen cleaning up the centre of town.

Monks flown in from Battambang city congregated at the pagoda in Pailin to plan for Tuesday's ceremony, while an army general, Phon Savath, was seen on Monday morning rehearsing speeches and saluting his Khmer Rouge counterpart ahead of the real thing.
The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N.-brokered peace pact with rival factions in 1991 but later reneged on the accord and continued to fight the coalition that emerged from 1993 polls.
